column1: # EAST BERLIN, THE READING THAT WAS ONLY EVER AN ARGUMENT — TWO THIRDS OF IT IS NOW A READING.
# Landesarchiv Berlin LABSA, eleven East Berlin registry offices, death-index volumes 1990-1994.
# Work list row 253. Read 11 October 2026.
# WHY 1990 AND NOT 1980. Row 253's last unclosed reading was that AGNES LEIBHOLZ née KERGER died in
# East Berlin. The 8 October sweep left the East on the argument that "a West Berliner listed in a
# 1979 telephone book did not move to the DDR". THAT ARGUMENT IS RIGHT AND IT HAS A DATE ON IT:
# until 9 November 1989 a West Berlin pensioner could not relocate east at all. So the hypothesis is
# live only from 1990, when she was 101, to 1994, when the index closes and she would have been 105.
field
# ---------------- THE SLICE, AND IT WAS AFFORDABLE ----------------
the whole of East Berlin 1990-1994 is 47 volumes and one gigabyte
column2: against 605 volumes and 41.9 GB for the eleven offices entire. Scoping to the only years the hypothesis can live in turned an unaffordable sweep into an afternoon. ELEVEN OFFICES: Mitte, Prenzlauer Berg, Friedrichshain, Treptow, Köpenick, Lichtenberg, Weißensee, Pankow, Marzahn, Hohenschönhausen, Hellersdorf.

column1: and two of the eleven stop in 1990 regardless
column2: TREPTOW's death indexes end at P Rep. 635 Nr. 194 (1990) and HOHENSCHÖNHAUSEN's at P Rep. 323 Nr. 21 (1990). LABSA HOLDS NO 1991-1994 INDEX FOR EITHER BOROUGH. That is a holding limit, not an unread volume, and it cannot be closed by reading.

column1: *** 47 VOLUMES DOWNLOADED AND SCORED. THIRTY-THREE LEGIBLE AND READ. FOURTEEN BLIND AND NOT READ. ***
column2: the legible run scores 1.384 to 2.506 control names a page; the blind fourteen score 0.000, not one of them anywhere near the 0.15 threshold. THERE IS NOTHING IN BETWEEN, which is the same clean separation this archive has found in every series it has scored.

column1: *** NO LEIBHOLZ, NO LEIPHOLZ, NO LEIPSHOLZ, NO LUWINSKI AND NO LOWINSKI IN ANY OF THE THIRTY-THREE. ***
column2: and no Agnes Kerger. The search ran the family's spellings AND the maiden name KERGER, which is the first time that surname has been put to any East Berlin office.

column1: and Prenzlauer Berg is blind for four years, not one
column2: Nr. 968 (1990), 1059 (1991), 1101 (1992) and 1137 (1993) are all 0.000; only Nr. 1168 (1994) reads. One office out of eleven behaves differently from the other ten and nothing here explains why.

column1: *** WHICH IS A SCANNING BOUNDARY AT 1990/91, AND IT IS THE THIRD ONE THIS ARCHIVE HAS MEASURED ***
column2: Kreuzberg's text layer begins at 1963. Schöneberg's at 1984. East Berlin's at 1991. A DATE WHERE A SERIES CHANGES FROM ONE SCAN GENERATION TO ANOTHER IS A PROPERTY OF THE DIGITISATION AND NOT OF THE RECORDS, it differs per office, and it has to be measured each time rather than carried over.

column1: # ---------------- SO WHAT THE EAST BERLIN READING IS NOW WORTH ----------------
IT IS TWO THIRDS CLOSED AND SAID TO BE
column2: 1991 to 1994 is read and empty in nine of the eleven offices, and unavailable in the other two because the holding stops. 1990 IS UNREAD EVERYWHERE, and Prenzlauer Berg is unread to 1993.

column1: and the unread third is not being read, which is a judgement and is recorded as one
column2: the fourteen blind volumes are 1,759 pages. Read by L block at the image, as this archive read the four blind Kreuzberg years, that is perhaps fourteen band reads. IT IS NOT BEING DONE, because the prior does not carry it: the hypothesis requires a woman of 100 to leave the borough she had lived in for decades, cross a border that had been shut her whole adult life and had been open for weeks, and die in the east within five years. THE WORK IS SCOPED AND NAMED ABOVE so that anyone who disagrees can do it in an afternoon.

column1: *** AND THE L-BLOCK LIMIT WOULD APPLY TO IT, WHICH IS A SECOND REASON NOT TO PRETEND IT WOULD SETTLE ANYTHING ***
column2: the same limit found in Spandau 1980 the same day: a woman whose name of record is not the family's may be filed under her own initial and never cross-indexed. Reading fourteen L blocks would produce a negative of exactly the narrowness this archive has just finished writing a caution about.

column1: # ---------------- ONE KERGER, AND SHE IS NOT AGNES ----------------
KÖPENICK 1992 — "Kerger, Karoline Henriette Lucie"
column2: the only Kerger in the thirty-three legible volumes. AGNES WAS BORN 10 MARCH 1889 AND MARRIED A LEIBHOLZ; this woman carries three forenames, none of them Agnes, and no married name. NOT HER. The register number is not cleanly separable in the text layer and is not recorded rather than guessed. Written down so the surname is not searched again on the assumption it was never tried.

column1: near misses settled, so nobody settles them twice
column2: LEIB, Hildegard Martha Emma (Köpenick 1991 Nr. 883) · LEIBNER, Emma Gertrud Frida, also indexed as WILK geb. Leibner (Köpenick 1991 Nr. 1682) · LEIBNER, Charlotte Margarete Berta, also LIPPERT geb. Leibner (Köpenick 1992 Nr. 857) · LEIPNER, Erna Martha, also KIRBACH geb. Leipner (Köpenick 1992 Nr. 218) · LEIBIGER geb. Schönherr, Alma Anni (Köpenick 1992).

column1: and the Köpenick index cross-references every one of them both ways
column2: which is the behaviour Spandau did NOT show for Else Hedwig Herfert the same day. CROSS-INDEXING IS AN OFFICE'S HABIT AND NOT A RULE, and that is now observed in two directions rather than assumed in one.

column1: two readings, and neither is reachable today
column2: SHE DIED OUTSIDE BERLIN — unreachable without an address, and nothing held here gives one. OR SHE DIED AFTER 1994 — unreachable until the thirty-year closure moves, which for 1995 is 2025 and has already passed, so the LABSA holding may extend in time even if it has not yet. THE EAST BERLIN READING IS RETIRED as far as evidence can retire it.
